**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require compliance records before accepting POC-006 PASS**

When the new `local-v1` POC-006 route reaches a terminal PASS, this branch verifies only the `sourceValidationScope` literal. The execution schema permits an empty `complianceReviews` array, and `test_87_local_terminal_routes_and_shared_ai_protocol` builds exactly that fixture while setting the privacy/license booleans to `true`, so the checker accepts a result with no review reference or subject-version binding even though the plan requires approved records for the exact OpenList/WebDAV version. Require both review types, verify their referenced files, and match their subject versions before accepting PASS.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Qualify POC evidence contracts by acceptance profile**

When POC-006 (or another split-route POC) completes under `local-v1`, this supposedly scoped result still produces the unqualified `POC-06-EVIDENCE` contract. The result index and result record retain only one profile-agnostic terminal result per POC task, while GZ-020 depends on the same POC task and consumes the same unqualified contract; consequently a local PASS can make the production dependency appear complete, and there is no separate slot for a later production run without replacing completed evidence. Carry the profile into the result/index contract and require production-profile evidence for GZ-020, or create separate profile-specific tasks/contracts.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject POC-003 PASS when Range correctness is incomplete**

For a `local-v1` POC-003 execution, `range_correctness` is excluded from the boolean gates and the generic numeric validator accepts any finite value, so an execution reporting `0`, a negative percentage, or any value below complete byte-range correctness can still receive terminal PASS when the remaining booleans are true. This contradicts the route's exit criterion that responses match the requested byte intervals; validate the percentage domain and require the passing correctness threshold rather than treating it like an observational latency metric.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add a production verifier for heterogeneous compatibility**

When GZ-020 evaluates the production profile, this NFR is marked production-applicable but none of its listed verification owners can verify it on that profile: production executions of POC-001 and POC-002 select their original A380/ESXi protocols, which do not contain the heterogeneous worker, physical-host, Android, or cross-node measurements, while GZ-011 only defines the acceptance suite and GZ-020 is not listed as an owner. The production gate therefore either has to reuse a forbidden local-profile result or leave this required NFR unverifiable; add corresponding production measurements/ownership or restrict the NFR to the profile that actually measures it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve local-only environment capture requirements**

If a local route drops a local-only capture field such as POC-001's `physical_host_scope` or `android_validation_scope`, this check still passes because it only requires the original production capture fields to remain a subset. Since terminal validation derives its required environment directly from the now-weakened local list, the resulting PASS would no longer need evidence distinguishing WSL/same-host workers from physical hosts or tested Android devices. Define and enforce the required local capture fields per POC rather than checking only the common production subset.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate POC-004 PASS on authenticated Range and hash checks**

When POC-004 runs under `local-v1`, this exit gate requires real authenticated reads, Range handling, and hash verification, but the corresponding `localValidation.protocol.measurements` contains no authentication or Range-correctness gate, while `hash_mismatch_replica_rejected` only tests rejection of a bad copy. Since `validate_execution` accepts PASS based solely on the listed measurements, the terminal fixture in `test_87_local_terminal_routes_and_shared_ai_protocol` can pass without exercising these newly declared conditions; add explicit measurements and checker gates for them, or stop claiming them in this exit gate.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make same-wave POCs depend on GZ-021**

When POC-005—or similarly POC-003—is reserved while GZ-021 remains in progress, the transition gate permits it because these tasks are all in W2 and POC-005 still depends only on GZ-010. This newly declared `local-v1` OpenList route relies on the plan schema and checker delivered by GZ-021, so the POC can execute against the old `POC-PROTOCOL-V1` before the revision reaches `main`, leaving its evidence incompatible with the post-GZ-021 validator. Add GZ-021 to the affected same-wave POCs' `dependsOn` lists or move them to a later wave rather than relying on `integrationOrder`.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require a nonzero reservation in local capacity PASS**

When a local POC-004 execution configures `maxReservedBytes: 0` and reports `local_maximum_reserved_bytes: 0`, this condition accepts the configuration and the later PASS calculation can succeed. That makes the reservation portion of the capacity experiment vacuous: no in-flight output is ever reserved, despite NFR-V1-CAP-005 and the POC method requiring task-space reservations to be measured while exercising admission and eviction. Require a positive reservation budget and, for PASS, evidence of a positive observed reservation.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind local compliance reviews to the OpenList version**

For a `local-v1` POC-006 run, changing `openlist_version` while retaining the same `provider_api_or_sdk_version` still allows an older privacy/license approval to pass, because this function derives `subjectVersion` exclusively from the latter field. Fresh evidence in the current revision is that the newly added record validator checks the resulting value and scope but never incorporates the separately captured OpenList tool version, despite the local protocol requiring approval for the exact OpenList/WebDAV version tested. Bind the review to both relevant versions, or select `openlist_version` for this route.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep nested evidence refs inside the selected profile slot**

When a qualified result references raw output, resource configuration/booking, sample approval, profile configuration, or compliance evidence outside its versioned profile directory, this projection resets `evidencePath` to the owner's broad root (`evidence/POC-xxx` or `evidence/GZ-020`), so all subsequent `existing_ref` checks accept those unqualified files. A production POC can therefore reuse artifacts from another POC's directory, and a local result can reuse legacy evidence, despite `docs/18-testing-and-acceptance.md:21` and ADR-0015 requiring evidence to remain separated by POC/profile/version. Pass the selected slot prefix through nested-reference validation rather than widening it to the owner root.

For POC-009, changing `model_identity` or the provider/tool stack while retaining the same `model_version` leaves `subjectVersion` unchanged, so previously approved privacy and license records can be reused for a different model or provider and the qualified result still passes. Build the review subject from at least the captured model identity and version, plus any provider/tool version that controls licensing or data handling, as is already done for the composite POC-006 subject.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate numeric domains before accepting profile PASS**

When a qualified execution reports impossible numeric values, this profile gate can still accept PASS because downstream `good_actual` requires only a finite number. For example, a local-v1 POC-005 result with `file_count: -1`, negative directory counts, and negative rates passes once its boolean measurements are true, allowing GZ-018's required profile set to contain a meaningless scale experiment. Enforce metric domains such as nonnegative counts, sizes, durations, rates, and latencies—and bounded ratios/scores—before treating the profile result as an independently approved PASS.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align the Android NFR with the local profile**

When GZ-018 evaluates `local-v1`, this NFR is applicable and states that Android nodes must be actually validated, but the local POC-001 route explicitly permits Android-phone validation to remain untested: `android_validation_scope` may merely record that limitation, and no local measurement requires a real Android encode, thermal, power, or background-survival run. The checker can therefore approve all ten local profile results while this applicable frozen NFR remains unsatisfied; split the tested-node local constraint from the production Android obligation, restrict applicability, or require real Android evidence before local PASS.

A production POC can therefore qualify while its A380/TrueNAS booking file says `rejected`, or while the referenced configuration belongs to another resource or task. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind qualified executions to the tested source revision**

When evidence is executed against an older checkout and later committed alongside a newer implementation, this configuration check still accepts it because it binds only the task, profile, resources, and measurement IDs; none of the route capture lists or execution schemas requires an immutable source commit/tree. The same evidence can therefore continue granting qualified PASS after behavior changes, despite ADR-0015 requiring results to bind the actual source; require and validate a source revision in every qualified execution/configuration.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Permit sibling evidence in source-drift checks**

When `--milestone GZ-020` validates all ten production slots, the evidence for the other nine experiments necessarily appears in the diff from each execution's tested commit to the final HEAD. Because `own_prefixes` contains only the current POC's slot, those sibling paths under `evidence/GZ-020/poc/...` trigger this rejection; the same happens when all runs are prepared together as untracked files. Consequently independently recorded production runs cannot coexist in a passing full milestone unless the evidence already existed in the tested source commit, which would be circular. Exclude all task-owned GZ-020 evidence from source-drift detection while continuing to reject implementation changes.

When an execution supplies an ordered window entirely in the future, this function accepts it, and matching future resource approvals and a later future result approval can satisfy the remaining checks. Thus `--require-results` can grant a qualified PASS before any claimed command or measurement has occurred. Require `finishedAt` and approval timestamps to be no later than the validation time; only validity end dates should be permitted to remain in the future.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require a nonempty workload for POC-005 PASS**

When a local-v1 POC-005 execution reports `file_count: 0`, `directory_count: 0`, `enumeration_rate: 0`, and other zero-valued workload metrics, these nonnegative checks accept the record and the boolean measurements can still yield terminal PASS. That permits an empty synthetic hierarchy to satisfy the required scale experiment and enter the full local milestone without exercising enumeration or incremental scanning. Keep zero available for failure/inconclusive records if needed, but require a positive population and positive exercised work for PASS.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject dotted secret keys in qualified records**

When a qualified resource configuration uses a common dotted key such as `auth.token` or `api.key` with an opaque credential value, this scan accepts it: `normalize_key` preserves dots, while `secret_key` recognizes sensitive terms only at string or underscore boundaries, and the free-form `configuration` schema permits these keys. The profile can therefore receive PASS while committing a plaintext credential inside its approved configuration record. Normalize all non-alphanumeric separators before matching, or constrain configuration records to Secret references and explicitly reject credential-bearing fields.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require dedicated raw execution artifacts**

When an execution puts an existing resource configuration, booking, sample approval, or profile configuration path in both `rawOutputRefs` and a command's `outputRef`, the membership and file-existence checks succeed, and the same YAML can still pass its structured-record validation. The qualified result therefore needs no actual command output at all; even Android's `rawOutputRef` can reuse that file. Require raw outputs to be disjoint from configuration and approval references and bind each artifact by type and checksum before accepting PASS.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind output hashes to produced media bytes**

For a qualified POC-002 PASS, this hashes each raw evidence artifact but never compares any artifact digest with `provenance.output_sha256`. An execution can therefore provide an arbitrary nonempty command log, set `output_sha256` to any syntactically valid digest, and assert `encode_provenance_complete: true`, even though `POC-002.yaml:271-276` requires verification against the produced media bytes. Require a designated produced-media artifact and match its computed digest to the provenance hash before accepting PASS.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the POC-002 worker inventory before PASS**

When a qualified POC-002 execution supplies `worker_node_inventory`, `physical_host_scope`, and `encoder_capability_matrix` as arbitrary non-placeholder strings—or describes only one unqualified node—this function returns without validating them because structured worker checks are limited to POC-001. The POC-002 boolean measurements can then grant PASS without proving the Windows/Linux worker pool or actual multi-node parallel AV1 execution required by `program-plan.yaml:251-252` and `POC-002.yaml:306-312`; require a typed inventory with the expected tested platforms/nodes and bind the execution artifacts to those identities.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require a nonzero POC-002 workload for PASS**

For either qualified POC-002 profile, `encode_throughput: 0` is accepted as a valid stream count and `sustained_encode_duration: 0` is accepted as a valid duration, with no later PASS-specific check requiring either value to be positive. Once the boolean fields are asserted true, an execution that performed no sustained encode workload can therefore satisfy the profile and enter a full milestone despite the protocol requiring a concurrency sweep and recorded soak run; retain zero for fail/inconclusive records if needed, but require positive throughput and duration for PASS.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject ignored files as qualified evidence**

When a qualified execution references an ignored file such as `evidence/POC-002/profiles/local-v1/v1/encode.log`, all existence, size, and checksum checks can pass locally, but this command omits it because `.gitignore` excludes `*.log`. The validator can therefore approve evidence that is absent from the commit and from a reviewer's clean checkout. Require every referenced qualified-evidence file to be tracked, or explicitly detect ignored untracked files rather than using `--exclude-standard`.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Hash large evidence artifacts incrementally**

When real POC evidence contains large media or large-file transfer artifacts, `read_bytes()` loads each entire artifact into memory; POC-002 outputs are then read again for the provenance and per-worker checks. A sufficiently large but valid artifact can therefore exhaust memory and make the mandatory acceptance validator unusable. Use `stat()` for the size and stream the SHA-256 calculation in bounded chunks, reusing the resulting digest in later checks.

The qualified PASS can therefore claim temperature, power, and background-survival measurements without retaining the observation data needed to reproduce them; require a distinct `scope_observation` artifact bound to the tested node/device rather than accepting an arbitrary raw reference.
